rows.stem: The number of shells required to write the electronic configuration of Potassium (At. No. 19)
rows.solution:
Potassium has 19 electrons, arranged as 2, 8, 8, 1. These fill the K, L and M shells and put one electron in the N shell, so four shells are needed.

This is option (D) 4.

rows.stem: Which of the following is an alloy of copper and tin ?
rows.solution:
Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc, nichrome of nickel and chromium (with iron), and constantan of copper and nickel.

This is option (D) Bronze.

rows.stem: Tooth decay begins at the pH of :
rows.solution:
Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth falls below 5.5: bacteria act on sugar and food particles left in the mouth and produce acids, and tooth enamel (calcium hydroxyapatite) begins to corrode. Of the given values, only 5.1 is below 5.5.

This is option (A) 5.1.

rows.stem: Which one of the following organism is represented by this diagram ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the organism exists only as a boxed drawing (several thin upright stalks, each ending in a rounded dotted head, rising from a branching base, with one head releasing particles labelled 'Spores'); the stem names nothing, and naming the organism here would state the answer. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
The drawing shows thread-like hyphae with thin upright stalks, each ending in a rounded head (a sporangium) that releases spores. This is the bread mould Rhizopus, which reproduces by spore formation. When the spores land on a moist surface, each can grow into a new Rhizopus.

This is option (D) Rhizopus.

rows.stem: S.I. unit of electrical resistivity is
rows.solution:
The resistance of a conductor is \(R = \rho \dfrac{l}{A}\), so \(\rho = \dfrac{RA}{l}\). Its unit is

\(\dfrac{\Omega \times \mathrm{m^2}}{\mathrm{m}} = \Omega\,\mathrm{m}\),

that is, ohm metre.

This is option (C) ohm . metre.

rows.stem: The minimum resistance which can be made using five resistors each of resistance \(10\,\Omega\) is :
rows.solution:
The resistance is least when all five resistors are joined in parallel:

\(\dfrac{1}{R} = 5 \times \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), so \(R = 2\,\Omega\).

This is option (C) \(2\,\Omega\).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Metals in the middle of activity series are found in nature as sulphides or carbonates.

**Reason (R) :** The sulphide ores are calcinated whereas carbonate ores are roasted to extract metals from them.
rows.context: These questions consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
Metals in the middle of the activity series, such as iron, zinc, lead and copper, are moderately reactive and are usually found in nature as their sulphides or carbonates. The Assertion is true.

It is the other way round: sulphide ores are roasted (heated strongly in excess air) and carbonate ores are calcinated (heated strongly in limited air), each to change the ore into an oxide. So the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem: Define a decomposition reaction. Write an equation to show thermal decomposition of ferrous sulphate crystals.
rows.solution:
A decomposition reaction is one in which a single reactant breaks down to give two or more simpler products.

On heating, green ferrous sulphate crystals first lose their water of crystallisation, and the ferrous sulphate then decomposes into ferric oxide, sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide, with the smell of burning sulphur:

\(\mathrm{2FeSO_4(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Fe_2O_3(s) + SO_2(g) + SO_3(g)}\)

rows.stem: What is meant by a balanced chemical equation ? Why is it necessary for the equation to be balanced ?
rows.solution:
A balanced chemical equation is one in which the total number of atoms of each element is the same on the reactant side and on the product side.

An equation must be balanced because of the law of conservation of mass: mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction, so the total mass of the products must equal the total mass of the reactants.

rows.stem:
Two test tubes A and B are taken, each containing one mL of starch solution. Add 1 mL of saliva to test tube ‘A’ only and leave both the test tubes undisturbed for a few minutes. Now add a few drops of dilute iodine solution to both the test tubes.

(a) Which one of the two test tubes shows change in colour ? Write the changed colour observed in this test tube.

(b) What can we conclude from this activity ?
rows.solution:
(a) Test tube B shows the change: its colour turns blue-black.

(b) Saliva contains an enzyme (salivary amylase) that breaks starch down into sugar. In test tube A the starch has been digested, so iodine gives no blue-black colour. Test tube B had no saliva, so its starch remains and gives the blue-black colour with iodine. So saliva digests starch.

rows.stem: Name two types of germ cells present in human beings. List two structural differences between the two.
rows.solution:
The two types of germ cells are the egg (ovum) in the female and the sperm in the male.

Any two structural differences:

| Egg (ovum) | Sperm |
|---|---|
| Large in size | Small in size |
| Spherical in shape | Elongated, with a long tail |
| Non-motile | Motile |

rows.stem:
(a) In angiosperms why fertilisation cannot take place in flowers if pollination does not take place ? Where is zygote located in a flower after fertilisation ? What does it develop into ?

(b) Write the names of those parts of a flower which serve the same function as the following do in animals :

(i) testis (ii) ovary
rows.solution:
(a) In angiosperms the male germ cells are in the pollen grains, while the female germ cell is in the ovule inside the ovary. Unless pollination transfers the pollen grains from the anther to the stigma, no pollen tube can grow down the style to the ovule, so the male germ cell never reaches the female germ cell and fertilisation cannot take place.

After fertilisation the zygote is located in the ovule (inside the ovary). It develops into the embryo, and the ovule develops into the seed.

(b) (i) Testis: the anther (of the stamen), which produces the pollen grains.

(ii) Ovary: the ovary (of the pistil), which contains the ovules.

rows.stem:
(a) State any two observations when an electric current is passed through acidulated water, in a container having each electrode covered by test tubes filled with water.

(b) Write the ratio of the mass of the gas collected at the cathode to the mass of the gas collected at the anode.
rows.solution:
(a) Any two:

1. Bubbles of gas form at both the electrodes.

2. The gas displaces the water in both the test tubes.

3. The volume of gas collected at the cathode is twice the volume collected at the anode.

(b) Electrolysis of water gives hydrogen at the cathode and oxygen at the anode:

\(\mathrm{2H_2O(l) \xrightarrow{\text{electricity}} 2H_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

So 2 molecules of hydrogen form for every molecule of oxygen. Their masses are in the ratio

\(2 \times 2 : 1 \times 32 = 4 : 32 = 1 : 8\).

The mass of hydrogen at the cathode to the mass of oxygen at the anode is \(1 : 8\).

rows.stem: An object is placed in front of a concave mirror of focal length 12 cm. If distance of the object from the pole of the mirror is 8 cm, then use mirror formula to determine the position of the image formed. Draw a labelled ray diagram to justify your answer in this case.
rows.solution:
For a concave mirror, \(f = -12\) cm and \(u = -8\) cm. The mirror formula gives

\(\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{-2 + 3}{24} = \dfrac{1}{24}\).

So \(v = +24\) cm: the image is formed 24 cm behind the mirror. It is virtual and erect, and enlarged (\(m = -\dfrac{v}{u} = -\dfrac{24}{-8} = 3\)).

Ray diagram: draw the concave mirror with its pole P, the focus F (12 cm from P) and the centre of curvature C (24 cm from P) on the principal axis, and the object AB at 8 cm, between P and F. From the top of the object draw a ray parallel to the principal axis; after reflection it passes through F. Draw a second ray from the top of the object along the line from C, so that it falls normally on the mirror and is reflected back along itself. The two reflected rays diverge; produce them backwards (dotted) behind the mirror, where they meet at B'. Drop a perpendicular A'B' to the axis at A', 24 cm behind the mirror: the image A'B' is virtual, erect and larger than the object. Draw arrows on the rays.

rows.stem:
(i) The image of an object formed by a mirror is real, inverted and is of magnification-1. If the image is at a distance of 30 cm from the mirror, where is the object placed ? Give reason to justify your answer.

(ii) Where would the image be if the object is moved 15 cm towards the mirror ? Draw ray diagram for the new position of the object to justify your answer.
rows.solution:
(i) The image is real and inverted with magnification \(-1\), so it is the same size as the object. A concave mirror forms such an image only when the object is at its centre of curvature C, and the image is then also at C. Since \(m = -\dfrac{v}{u} = -1\), the image distance equals the object distance. The image is 30 cm from the mirror, so the object is placed 30 cm in front of the mirror, at C. (So the radius of curvature is 30 cm and the focal length is 15 cm.)

(ii) Moving the object 15 cm towards the mirror places it at 15 cm, which is the focus F. Using the mirror formula with \(u = -15\) cm and \(f = -15\) cm:

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{15} = 0\),

so the image is formed at infinity (real, inverted and highly enlarged).

Ray diagram: draw the concave mirror with P, F and C on the principal axis and the object AB standing at F. From the top of the object draw a ray parallel to the principal axis; after reflection it passes through F. Draw a second ray from the top of the object along the line from C, which is reflected back along itself. The two reflected rays are parallel to each other, so they meet only at infinity. Draw arrows on the rays.

rows.stem:
(a) State Fleming’s left hand rule. Apply this rule to determine the direction of force experienced by a straight current carrying conductor AB placed in a uniform magnetic field as shown.

(b) What will happen to an electron which enters in the same field in the same direction in which the current is flowing in the conductor AB ? Give reason to justify your answer.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the directions exist only in the drawing: a straight vertical conductor with end A at the top and B at the bottom, an arrow on it labelled 'Electric Current', crossed by four parallel horizontal field lines with arrowheads, labelled 'Magnetic field'. Which way the current and the field point is withheld here because it fixes the answer. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
(a) Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, the thumb points in the direction of motion of, or the force on, the conductor.

In the figure the current in AB flows upwards (from B to A) and the magnetic field points from left to right. Point the forefinger to the right and the middle finger upwards: the thumb then points into the page. So the force on the conductor AB is perpendicular to the page, directed into it (vertically downwards if the page lies flat).

(b) The electron is deflected in the opposite direction, out of the page (vertically upwards if the page lies flat). The direction of current is the direction of flow of positive charge, so an electron moving upwards is equivalent to a current flowing downwards, opposite to the current in AB. Reversing the current reverses the force, so the electron experiences a force out of the page.
